correctness.rationale: Cauchy–Schwarz on the 21 projective lines and maximality bounds unmatched-shore size by six and forces six-point hyperovals at equality; the residual 3-regular bipartite graph has perfect matchings by Hall. Complete incidence enumeration finds 168 hyperovals and 288 perfect matchings for each. Independently constructed affine C++17 and homogeneous-coordinate Python/NumPy checkers exhaust all 3,360 eligible pairs of fibers and all 82,944 matching pairs per fiber pair. They find exactly zero six-edge bridges and 216 seven-edge bridges per pair, verify quotient and within-fiber connectivity, and reproduce all 1,669,248 exchange edges and 67/71 vertex degrees. This is a finite exact proof, not asymptotic inference.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Spiro–Adriaensen–Mattheus proves gamma_e=15 for the plane and maximal-arc equality, but neither it nor the fixed 288-matching Tutte–Coxeter reconfiguration theorem specifies transitions between distinct unmatched six-point/line configurations. The latter is a proper induced subgraph of the 48,384-state global exchange graph and does not dominate its connectivity claim.

value.rationale: The 168 natural unmatched-hyperoval fibers each consist of 288 minimum matching placements, but local four-edge mobility never overcomes the geometric obstruction between fibers. Establishing sharp seven-edge global mobility and counting 216 transitions per quotient edge is an exact structural reconfiguration classification of a classical finite geometry, addressing the natural ability to change optimal matchings while preserving minimality. The new global exchange-degree distribution identifies two distinct local mobility types and cannot be inferred from static optimizer counts.
